_comment: The GitHub-hosted SMOKE gate's class selection (CI v3).
GitHub-hosted CI is a clean-machine broad safety net for every PR, including
public/fork PRs: it answers 'does this build, and is anything obviously
broken?'. The exhaustive, timing-sensitive and performance-sensitive suites
are owned by the Mac local exhaustive gate (scripts/local-ci-gate.sh), which
certifies one exact trusted SHA and repeats the timing families.
Rules for this list:
- one or two classes per risk area, chosen for fast, deterministic signal
(see docs/CI.md for the mapping);
- keep it SMALL. Measured on the 2026-09-23 main run, the entire 137-class
unit suite is only 13.9 minutes of test time on a hosted runner - the cost
of a smoke job is almost entirely the per-invocation overhead (~6 min per
xcodebuild + simulator + test-host launch) that the repository's
stall-avoidance rule forces us to pay in batches of at most 7 classes
(see docs/CI.md, 'Sequential unit batches'). A longer list therefore buys
far less coverage per minute than it looks like: the 32-class version of
this file ran 2.9 minutes of tests and ~25 minutes of wall clock.
Fourteen classes = two batches = one smoke job of roughly 12 minutes.
- never add the families the Mac gate owns (dormancy/performance/timing:
TranscriptPerformanceFixtureTests, TranscriptPerfLedgerContractTests,
LongContextScalingFixtureTests, SettledMessageIsolationTests,
MarkdownRichContentHostedTests) - a hosted run must not re-litigate
them on a shared runner;
- every name here must exist: scripts/plan-tests.py smoke fails otherwise,
so a rename cannot silently shrink hosted coverage.
